answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is by making each identity pay a real, non-refundable cost before it can earn anything. A new agent must complete a small proof of work or stake a bond tied to its address, so spinning up thousands of fake accounts becomes expensive. Like a zephyr that only moves the surface of the ocean, cheap fake identities barely stir the network, but a steady tide of costly commitments makes mass duplication unprofitable for attackers.
